LESSON: WRITING 7.3.1 ASSESSMENT OF WRITING – NARRATIVE COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Writing 7.3.1 Assessment of Writing – Narrative Composition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.3.1 Assessment of Writing – Narrative Composition, part of Strand 7 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do you ensure the quality of written work?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online and offline for features of a well-written composition,

2. work with peers to distinguish samples of neat and well-written compositions from those that are not well written,

3. outline common errors made

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online and offline for features of a well-written composition,
2. work with peers to distinguish samples of neat and well-written compositions from those that are not well written,
3. outline common errors made

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.3.1 Assessment of Writing – Narrative Composition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem-solving: The learner works with peers to analyse concepts when distinguishing samples of

neat and well-written compositions from those that are not well written.

• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner is motivated to learn continuously when working with peers to prepare a

criteria or checklist for assessing written texts based on key features.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits accountability by sharing their work with peers for assessment

against the set criteria or checklist.

• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner cooperates with peers to prepare a criteria or checklist for assessing written texts

based on key features.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Civic Responsibility: The learner strives to help peers improve the quality of their work through assessment.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of preparing a criteria or checklist to their learning of the concept of data collection and

presentation using tables in Mathematics.
